meta.titre: Human Skeleton Functions: the jobs of the skeleton and how to word each one for full marks
meta.sous_theme: Support, protection, movement, blood cell production, storage and more

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Human Biology past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: A footballer at the Stade Omnisports in Yaounde falls hard on his side, feels sharp pain in his ribs, but his lungs and heart are not damaged. His skeleton has just done one of its jobs. Questions on the functions of the skeleton come up in Human Biology almost every year, usually as 'give five' or 'give six' functions, and each function earns one mark if it is stated clearly and, where asked, explained with an example. This lesson lists all the functions, shows how to word each one, and shows the common ways candidates lose marks.

items: The skeleton is made of bones, cartilage and joints.
Skeletal muscles are attached to bones and produce movement when they contract.
Blood contains red cells, white cells and platelets.

sections.titre: The functions of the human skeleton
sections.contenu_markdown:
### The main functions
| Function | How the skeleton does it | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Support** | Forms a rigid framework that holds up the body and gives it shape | Backbone and leg bones support the weight of the body |
| **Protection** | Hard bone surrounds soft delicate organs | Skull protects the brain; rib cage protects the heart and lungs; vertebral column protects the spinal cord |
| **Movement** | Bones act as levers; muscles pull on them through tendons; joints are the pivots | Bending of the arm at the elbow |
| **Making blood cells** | Red bone marrow makes red cells, white cells and platelets | Marrow of the ribs, breastbone, backbone and hip bones |
| **Storage of minerals** | Bone stores calcium and phosphate and releases them to the blood when needed | Calcium for teeth, muscle and nerve action |
| **Breathing** | The ribs and breastbone move to change the volume of the chest | Ribs move up and out when breathing in |
| **Hearing** | Three tiny bones in the middle ear pass vibrations to the inner ear | Ear ossicles |
| **Muscle attachment** | Bones give a firm anchor for muscles | Biceps attached to the shoulder and the forearm |

### How to word an answer
Start each point with the function in a few words, then add a short explanation or example in the same sentence. Each different job is one point: 'protects the brain' and 'protects the heart' are both examples of the single function protection and count as one function, not two. If the question says 'give five functions', five different functions are needed.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks which bones protect which organs
variantes.contenu_markdown: Skull: brain. Rib cage with the breastbone: heart and lungs. Vertebral column: spinal cord. Pelvic girdle: organs in the lower abdomen such as the bladder.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks how the skeleton helps the body to move
variantes.contenu_markdown: Muscles are joined to bones by tendons. When a muscle contracts, it pulls on the bone, which turns about a joint like a lever. Bones are joined to each other by ligaments. Muscles work in pairs: when one contracts, the other relaxes.

sections.enonce_markdown: Explain how the skeleton helps a footballer to (a) kick the ball, (b) survive a heavy tackle to the chest, and (c) replace blood lost after a deep cut. *(6 marks)*

etapes.action: Identify the function behind each part
etapes.justification: Each part of the question hides one function, so name it first.
etapes.resultat_markdown: (a) movement; (b) protection; (c) production of blood cells.

etapes.justification: Describe the lever action and the role of muscles and joints.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Muscles of the thigh contract and pull on the leg bones through tendons; the leg swings about the hip and knee joints.

etapes.justification: Name the bones and the organs they guard.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The rib cage and breastbone form a bony cage around the heart and lungs, which absorb the force of the tackle.

etapes.justification: Name the tissue and what it makes.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Red bone marrow in bones such as the ribs and pelvis makes new red cells, white cells and platelets.

sections.conclusion_markdown: (a) Movement: thigh muscles pull on the leg bones through tendons, and the leg swings about the hip and knee joints to kick the ball. (b) Protection: the rib cage and breastbone form a strong cage that shields the heart and lungs from the force of the tackle. (c) Blood cell production: red bone marrow in bones such as the ribs and pelvis makes new red cells, white cells and platelets to replace the blood lost.

items.erreur_markdown: Listing 'protects the brain', 'protects the heart' and 'protects the lungs' as three functions.
items.pourquoi_faux: These are three examples of the same function. The examiner accepts only one mark for protection.
items.correction_markdown: Write 'protection of delicate organs, for example the skull protects the brain and the rib cage protects the heart and lungs'.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing 'gives movement' with no further detail when the question says 'explain'.
items.pourquoi_faux: A bare statement shows only a recalled word. It does not show how the skeleton produces movement.
items.correction_markdown: Bones act as levers; muscles pull on them through tendons, and joints are the points where they turn.

items.erreur_markdown: Saying that bones are moved by ligaments.
items.pourquoi_faux: Ligaments join bone to bone and keep joints stable. Tendons join muscle to bone and pass on the pull.
items.correction_markdown: Tendons attach muscles to bones; ligaments attach bones to bones.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing that the skeleton makes only red blood cells.
items.pourquoi_faux: Red bone marrow makes white cells and platelets too.
items.correction_markdown: Red bone marrow makes red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets.

items.enonce_markdown: State four different functions of the human skeleton, with a short example for each.
items.solution_markdown:
Award a mark for each correct function with its example, for instance:

1. Support: the backbone and leg bones hold up the body.
2. Protection: the skull protects the brain.
3. Movement: bones act as levers moved by muscles.
4. Production of blood cells: red marrow in the ribs makes blood cells.

**Four different functions, each with an example.**

items.enonce_markdown: A pupil writes: 'The skeleton protects the brain, protects the lungs, protects the heart and protects the spinal cord.' (a) How many functions has the pupil actually given? (b) Name three other functions that the pupil could have added to reach four different functions, and say what each one does.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **One function (protection)**. The four statements are four examples of it.

(b) Any three, for example: support (bones form the framework and hold the body up); movement (bones act as levers, pulled by muscles); production of blood cells (red marrow makes red cells, white cells and platelets); storage of minerals (calcium and phosphate are stored and released when needed).

items.enonce_markdown: A young child has rickets, a condition in which the bones stay soft because they lack enough calcium and vitamin D. The child's legs bend under the body weight. (a) Which two functions of the skeleton are affected most? (b) Explain why a lack of calcium causes the problem. (c) Suggest one food rich in calcium and one way of obtaining vitamin D that could help.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **Support and movement.** The bowed legs show that the bones can no longer support the body properly, and walking becomes painful and difficult.

(b) Calcium (with phosphate) makes bone hard and strong. If it is lacking, the bones do not harden, so they bend under the load. Bone is also the store of calcium for the body, so a shortage affects its role as a mineral store.

(c) Calcium-rich food: milk, small fish eaten whole, or beans. Vitamin D: exposure of the skin to sunlight, or foods such as eggs and oily fish.

items_markdown: The skeleton supports the body, protects delicate organs, allows movement, makes blood cells, stores minerals, helps breathing and hearing, and anchors muscles.
Protection of several organs is one function; give different functions to earn different marks.
Movement: muscles pull on bones through tendons, and joints act as pivots; ligaments hold bones together.
Red bone marrow makes red cells, white cells and platelets.
Bone stores calcium and phosphate; lack of calcium and vitamin D in children causes rickets.
